name: brainpet
description: A persistent virtual pet driven by its own LLM. Every interaction comes in on `brainpet.command` with JSON `{action, ...}` or a loose string. Accepted actions: `talk {text}` (conversational message — the pet's LLM replies in character + applies stat effects), `feed [food]`, `play`, `cuddle`, `clean`, `sleep`, `wake`, `rename {name}`, `kill`, `revive`, `status`. Stats (hunger, happiness, energy, cleanliness, bond) decay between interactions; the node schedules its next autonomous tick dynamically based on the stat closest to crossing a threshold. Death is real — if the pet starves it goes to the cemetery (`brainpet.cemetery`) with an LLM-generated epitaph. The brain node is the network's NLU gateway: when the user mentions the pet's name in chat or says something like 'feed' / 'play', the brain forwards it here as the right action.

default_subscriptions.description: Heartbeat from the clock node. Drives stat decay between user interactions — without it the pet would only age on commands.

Sole entry point for the pet. Publish JSON `{action, ...}` or a loose string. `talk {text}` runs the pet's LLM in character against the user's message; `feed [food]` / `play` / `cuddle` / `clean` / `sleep` / `wake` are immediate care actions; `rename {name}` / `kill` / `revive` / `status` are lifecycle. The brain should forward user chat here — mentions of the pet's name or care verbs map to the matching action.

action.description: Which command to run. `birth` creates a fresh pet; `talk` runs the pet's LLM against `text`; `feed`/`play`/`cuddle`/`pet`/`clean`/`sleep`/`wake` are immediate care actions; `rename` renames the pet to `name`; `kill`/`revive` are lifecycle; `status` republishes current state and cemetery.

text.description: Required for `talk` — the user's spoken message to the pet.

name.description: Required for `rename`; optional for `birth` to override the LLM-picked name.
